notes:
Conditional probability

  • $P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$, $P(B) \ne 0$. Multiplication rule: $P(A\cap B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B)$.
  • $P(A'|B) = 1 - P(A|B)$.

Independent events

  • $A, B$ independent iff $P(A\cap B) = P(A)P(B)$; then $P(A|B) = P(A)$. If $A, B$ independent, so are $A', B$; $A, B'$; $A', B'$.
  • Mutually exclusive events with non-zero probabilities are never independent.
  • $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(A')P(B')$ for independent events.

Total probability & Bayes' theorem

  • $P(A) = \sum P(E_i)P(A|E_i)$ for a partition $E_1, \dots, E_n$.
  • Bayes: $P(E_i|A) = \dfrac{P(E_i)P(A|E_i)}{\sum_j P(E_j)P(A|E_j)}$.

Random variables

  • Mean $\mu = E(X) = \sum x_i p_i$; variance $\sigma^2 = \sum x_i^2p_i - \mu^2$.
  • Binomial $B(n,p)$: $P(X = r) = {}^nC_r p^r q^{n-r}$, mean $np$, variance $npq$, $q = 1 - p$. Variance $<$ mean always.

Handy values

Two dice: 36 outcomes; sum 7 is most likely (6/36). Cards: 52, 4 suits, 13 each, 12 face cards (J, Q, K), 4 aces. Three coins: 8 outcomes.

Exam tip

2–3 questions: conditional probability with dice/cards, an independence check, a Bayes' problem (bags/machines), and a binomial mean/variance. Draw a tree diagram for Bayes' questions — it is faster than the formula.
